decision: Retain the symmetric readout as an offline candidate. It fixes mask-label dependence exactly and improves pooled raw corner F1 slightly, but some corners disappear, fine boundary localization can worsen, and real printed-paper false proposals remain. Do not integrate it as a hard graph filter or claim improved template recovery.
method: Use the same frozen MobileNetV3 proposal model on original and complemented binary masks with identical RGB. Average its Float16 sigmoid fields in Float32, round once to Float16, and apply the original thresholds. No new weights, per-image choices, threshold tuning or solver calls.

findings: The average often removes or moves duplicate synthetic corner responses and gives a small pooled gain. It does not uniformly preserve all true corners.

The largest reviewed loss, channel-755429-v2, loses one of two corners under averaging. Its two phase peaks are five pixels apart; individual scores are about 0.411 and 0.403, while the averaged score within three pixels of the reference is at most 0.353, below the unchanged 0.4 threshold.
The other two selected losses retain both corners but add a false proposal along a straight edge. Selected gains remove duplicate edge proposals or recover a near-threshold corner.

On real photographs, the stable mean still proposes corners on printed trees, stars, lettering, floral ink, and smooth petal/crescent/heart arcs. Wrong fixed crops still include packaging, background or reflective fragments.

The mean preserves many obvious grid corners and motif details, but these real photos have no complete junction annotations, so their proposal counts do not establish accuracy or improved legal templates.

rootCausesAndLimits: Exact symmetrization removes arbitrary label dependence, but averaging spatially displaced peaks can reduce both below a fixed detection threshold. The largest-loss replay reproduces all three original Float16 fields exactly and identifies this mechanism without changing crop, labels or model weights.

The existing 9px refinement improves lattice development F1 but reduces F1 on both recipe groups for every readout. Its earlier selection on development does not establish a universal localization benefit; raw and refined results remain separate.

The ideal-target decoding diagnostic recovers all 2544 reference corners across all 308 synthetic views. It rules out a target/peak-decoder mismatch on this cohort; it is not a general theorem or an upper bound on learned recall.
Mask-label consistency and material recognition are separate problems. Symmetric averaging cannot teach a model which printed edges belong to one sheet.

idealTargetDecode.timing: Post-hoc diagnostic after inspecting close reference corners; did not select a method or threshold.
idealTargetDecode.method: Decode the exact existing Gaussian target using the unchanged peak detector and 0.4 threshold; score against original visible junctions.
idealTargetDecode.limitation: This is target/decoder consistency, not an upper bound on learned recall or a change to the reference labels.

validation.scope: Existing tested boundary metrics, independent maximum-flow corner assignments, exact reference/control replays, all real field averages, every declared cohort, and complete selected visual review. No new application/core/model files or acceptance limits changed.

nextDirection: Train the proposal model with consistent targets under both mask-label phases, and add printed-paper examples whose reference labels remain the physical sheet boundaries. Keep the original evaluation sets and evaluate raw proposals before any local refinement. Full graph construction and editable-template tests are still required before release.
limitations: These recipe cohorts have been repeatedly inspected and are not topology-disjoint holdouts.
Reference visible corners exclude ambiguous hidden shared anchors; they do not uniquely supervise a full cut graph.
Averaging can suppress true peaks as well as false ones. Exact phase consistency alone is not evidence of better corner accuracy.
No solver or production change in this component study.
Real-photo labels remain unavailable; visual inspection is separate from synthetic reference metrics.
